verdict.rationale: Skyvern's docs say you give it a natural-language goal and a starting URL, and it navigates unseen sites, fills forms and completes multi-step tasks through an API or SDK. The GitHub README backs this up by describing mapping of visual elements to actions without custom code. One hands-on report says it handled the Geico happy path well but failed to click a popup on costcotravel.com, which points to uneven reliability on complex flows. missing for 10: independent evidence of reliable completion on complex or non-happy-path flows, and documented success-rate or benchmark data.

support.subject: As a developer, I can hand the product a natural-language goal and it completes a multi-step web task end to end — navigating, filling forms, and clicking through flows

citations.quote: You provide a natural-language prompt describing the goal, a starting URL, and optionally a JSON schema for structured output.
It navigates websites it has never seen before, filling forms, extracting data, and completing multi-step tasks via a simple API.
Skyvern can operate on websites it's never seen before, as it's able to map visual elements to actions necessary to complete a workflow, without any customized code
You send Skyvern a prompt and a URL, Skyvern runs a cloud browser, and you get structured output back.
